# firecrawl crawl

Bulk extract content from a website. Crawls pages following links up to a depth/limit.

**Prerequisite:** `crawl` requires authentication (no keyless free tier); without credentials the CLI prompts an interactive login.

## Quick start

```bash
# Crawl a docs section
firecrawl crawl "<url>" --include-paths /docs --limit 50 --wait -o .firecrawl/crawl.json

# Full crawl with depth limit
firecrawl crawl "<url>" --max-depth 3 --wait --progress -o .firecrawl/crawl.json

# Check status of a running crawl
firecrawl crawl <job-id>
```

Run `firecrawl crawl --help` for the full option list.

**Done when:** the crawl reaches a terminal status and the saved output under `.firecrawl/` contains the expected pages.

## Tips

- Use `--wait` when you need the results immediately. It has no default timeout; use `--timeout <seconds>` to bound polling. Without `--wait`, crawl returns a job ID for async polling.
- **One crawl, not a scrape loop.** If you're about to scrape a third page from the same site or section, crawl it instead with `--limit`.
- **Scope crawls with `--include-paths`** whenever the request names a section — crawl only the pages you need.
- Crawl consumes credits per page. Check `firecrawl credit-usage` before large crawls (`credit-usage` requires authentication).

## See also

- [firecrawl-scrape](../firecrawl-scrape/SKILL.md) — scrape individual pages
- [firecrawl-map](../firecrawl-map/SKILL.md) — discover URLs before deciding to crawl
- [firecrawl-download](../firecrawl-download/SKILL.md) — download site to local files (uses map + scrape)
- [firecrawl-build-scrape](https://github.com/firecrawl/skills/tree/main/skills/build/firecrawl-build-scrape) — building bulk extraction into an app instead of running it here

cd /tmp/fceval-s07-t1-64xmhhp_/work/.firecrawl && python3 -I -c "
import json,sys
d=json.load(open('crawl.json'))
print(type(d), list(d)[:10] if isinstance(d,dict) else len(d))
pages=d.get('data',d) if isinstance(d,dict) else d
print(d.get('status') if isinstance(d,dict) else '')
for p in pages:
    m=p.get('metadata',{})
    print('##',m.get('url') or m.get('sourceURL'),'|',m.get('title'),'|',(m.get('description') or '')[:200])
    print((p.get('markdown') or '')[:500].replace('\n',' '))
"

content.text:
I crawled 10 pages under `/features` (the cap). The full output is saved at `.firecrawl/crawl.json`.

1. **[SSO and SCIM](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/sso)**: Set up SAML/OIDC single sign-on and SCIM directory sync so your team signs in through your identity provider and access stays in sync.
2. **[Ask](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/ask)**: The `/support/ask` agentic support API, which diagnoses failed jobs and integration issues and returns actionable fix parameters.
3. **[Crawl](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/crawl)**: Recursively discovers and scrapes every reachable subpage of a site, handling sitemaps, JS rendering and rate limits.
4. **[PII Redaction](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/pii-redaction)**: Replaces personally identifiable information in scrape and parse markdown before it goes to agents, logs or vector stores.
5. **[Threat Protection](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/threat-protection)**: An organization-controlled policy, enforced server-side, that blocks requests to risky URLs across every endpoint.
6. **[Deep Research](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/alpha/deep-research)**: A legacy v1 alpha research API, being deprecated in favor of the Search API and the Deep Research use case.
7. **[Research Index](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/research)**: A purpose-built index for research agents, with tools to search papers, read full-text passages and find related work.
8. **[JSON mode](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/llm-extract)**: Uses an LLM to extract structured fields from a single URL. For multiple URLs or discovery, other tools are recommended.
9. **[Scrape](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/scrape)**: Turns any URL into clean, LLM-ready markdown, handling proxies, caching, rate limits and JS-heavy content.
10. **[IP Restrictions](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/ip-restrictions)**: Restricts a team's API keys to an allowlist of IPs or CIDR ranges, enforced server-side on every authenticated request.

Because of the 10-page cap, other pages under `/features` may exist that weren't fetched. I wrote these summaries from each page's title, description and opening text, not from the full content.
